# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""
Expert parallelism load balancer (EPLB) for vLLM.

This module implements the core rearrangement algorithm.

The rearrangement algorithm is adapted from
[DeepSeek EPLB](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/eplb).

Please find at [#12](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/EPLB/issues/12) an example
on how the EPLB algorithm works.
"""

# EVOLVE-BLOCK-START

import torch


def _try_threshold_pack(w_sorted: torch.Tensor, threshold: float,
                        slots_per_pack: int,
                        num_packs: int) -> torch.Tensor | None:
    """
    Feasibility check for a load threshold `threshold`.

    Items (rows of `w_sorted`, already sorted descending) are placed one at
    a time onto the least-loaded pack that (a) still has a free slot and
    (b) would stay at or below `threshold` after receiving the item. The
    loop is over items only; every op inside is vectorized across all rows
    (layers). Returns the pack index per sorted item, or None if any row
    cannot place all items under the threshold. Cardinality is exact by
    construction: all n = num_packs * slots_per_pack items are placed and
    no pack exceeds its slot budget.
    """
    x, n = w_sorted.shape
    device = w_sorted.device
    loads = torch.zeros(x, num_packs, dtype=w_sorted.dtype, device=device)
    counts = torch.zeros(x, num_packs, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    pack_sorted = torch.full((x, n), -1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    rows = torch.arange(x, device=device)
    big = torch.full_like(loads, float('inf'))
    eps = 1e-9
    for t in range(n):
        w_t = w_sorted[:, t:t + 1]
        elig = (counts < slots_per_pack) & (loads + w_t <= threshold + eps)
        if not bool(elig.any(-1).all()):
            return None
        j = torch.where(elig, loads, big).argmin(-1)
        pack_sorted[:, t] = j
        loads[rows, j] += w_sorted[:, t]
        counts[rows, j] += 1
    return pack_sorted


def balanced_packing(weight: torch.Tensor,
                     num_packs: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Pack n weighted objects to m packs, such that each bin contains exactly
    n/m objects and the weights of all packs are as balanced as possible.

    Approach: binary-search threshold feasibility packing (min-max makespan
    decision procedure). A cheap vectorized "serpentine" packing gives an
    upper bound on the achievable maximum pack load. We then bisect a load
    threshold T between the theoretical lower bound
    max(mean load, heaviest item) and the serpentine makespan; for each T a
    fully vectorized greedy feasibility pass (vectorized across all rows,
    sequential over sorted items) tries to place every item on a pack that
    keeps load <= T and respects the exact per-pack slot count. The lowest
    feasible T found yields the returned assignment, which is never worse
    than the serpentine fallback (used if bisection finds no improvement).

    Parameters:
        weight: [X, n], the weight of each item
        num_packs: number of packs

    Returns:
        pack_index: [X, n], the pack index of each item
        rank_in_pack: [X, n], the rank of the item in the pack
    """
    num_layers, num_groups = weight.shape
    assert num_groups % num_packs == 0
    groups_per_pack = num_groups // num_packs

    if groups_per_pack == 1:
        pack_index = torch.arange(num_groups, dtype=torch.int64,
                                  device=weight.device).expand(
                                      num_layers, num_groups)
        rank_in_pack = torch.zeros(num_layers, num_groups, dtype=torch.int64,
                                   device=weight.device)
        return pack_index, rank_in_pack

    # Sort items by weight, descending.
    indices = weight.sort(-1, descending=True).indices
    # Deal sorted items into blocks of num_packs; alternate block direction
    # (serpentine) so heavy items in consecutive blocks land on different
    # packs, approximating the greedy least-loaded strategy. Even blocks
    # deal packs 0..m-1, odd blocks deal m-1..0.
    pack_seq = torch.arange(num_packs, dtype=torch.int64,
                            device=weight.device)
    parity = (torch.arange(groups_per_pack, device=weight.device,
                           dtype=torch.int64).view(-1, 1) % 2) == 0
    pattern = torch.where(parity, pack_seq, pack_seq.flip(0))
    pack_sorted = pattern.reshape(1, num_groups).expand(num_layers,
                                                         num_groups)
    # Scatter back to original item positions.
    pack_index = torch.empty(num_layers, num_groups, dtype=torch.int64,
                             device=weight.device)
    pack_index.scatter_(1, indices, pack_sorted)

    # --- Bisection on the load threshold to minimize the max pack load ---
    w = weight.float()
    loads = torch.zeros(num_layers, num_packs, dtype=w.dtype,
                        device=w.device)
    loads.scatter_add_(1, pack_index, w)
    hi = float(loads.max())  # serpentine makespan (always feasible)
    lo = float(max(w.max().item(),
                   (w.sum(-1, keepdim=True) / num_packs).max().item()))
    best_sorted = None
    w_sorted = w.gather(-1, indices)
    if hi > lo * (1 + 1e-6):
        for _ in range(12):
            mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
            res = _try_threshold_pack(w_sorted, mid, groups_per_pack,
                                      num_packs)
            if res is not None:
                hi = mid
                best_sorted = res
            else:
                lo = mid
            if hi - lo <= 1e-9 * max(1.0, hi):
                break
    if best_sorted is not None:
        pack_index = torch.empty(num_layers, num_groups, dtype=torch.int64,
                                 device=weight.device)
        pack_index.scatter_(1, indices, best_sorted)

    # Recompute ranks so (pack_index, rank_in_pack) is a bijection onto
    # (pack, 0..groups_per_pack-1).
    item_ar = torch.arange(num_groups, dtype=torch.int64,
                           device=weight.device)
    order = (pack_index * num_groups + item_ar).argsort(-1)
    rank_in_pack = torch.empty_like(pack_index)
    rank_in_pack.scatter_(
        1, order,
        (item_ar % groups_per_pack).unsqueeze(0).expand(num_layers,
                                                        num_groups))
    return pack_index, rank_in_pack


def replicate_experts(
        weight: torch.Tensor,
        num_phy: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Replicate `num_log` experts to `num_phy` replicas, such that the maximum
    load of all replicas is minimized.

    Parameters:
        weight: [X, num_log]
        num_phy: total number of experts after replication

    Returns:
        phy2log: [X, num_phy], logical expert id of each physical expert
        rank: [X, num_phy], the replica rank
        logcnt: [X, num_log], number of replicas for each logical expert
    """
    n, num_log = weight.shape
    num_redundant = num_phy - num_log
    assert num_redundant >= 0
    device = weight.device
    phy2log = torch.arange(num_phy, dtype=torch.int64,
                           device=device).repeat(n, 1)
    rank = torch.zeros(n, num_phy, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    logcnt = torch.ones(n, num_log, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    arangen = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    for i in range(num_log, num_phy):
        redundant_indices = (weight / logcnt).max(dim=-1).indices
        phy2log[:, i] = redundant_indices
        rank[:, i] = logcnt[arangen, redundant_indices]
        logcnt[arangen, redundant_indices] += 1
    return phy2log, rank, logcnt


def rebalance_experts_hierarchical(
    weight: torch.Tensor,
    num_physical_experts: int,
    num_groups: int,
    num_nodes: int,
    num_gpus: int,
):
    """
    Parameters:
        weight: [num_moe_layers, num_logical_experts]
        num_physical_experts: number of physical experts after replication
        num_groups: number of expert groups
        num_nodes: number of server nodes, where the intra-node network
        (e.g, NVLink) is faster
        num_gpus: number of GPUs, must be a multiple of `num_nodes`

    Returns:
        physical_to_logical_map: [num_moe_layers, num_physical_experts]
        logical_to_physical_map: [num_moe_layers, num_logical_experts, X]
        logical_count: [num_moe_layers, num_logical_experts]
    """
    num_layers, num_logical_experts = weight.shape
    assert num_logical_experts % num_groups == 0
    group_size = num_logical_experts // num_groups
    assert num_groups % num_nodes == 0
    groups_per_node = num_groups // num_nodes
    assert num_gpus % num_nodes == 0
    assert num_physical_experts % num_gpus == 0
    phy_experts_per_gpu = num_physical_experts // num_gpus

    def inverse(perm: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        inv = torch.empty_like(perm)
        inv.scatter_(
            1,
            perm,
            torch.arange(perm.size(1), dtype=torch.int64,
                         device=perm.device).expand(perm.shape),
        )
        return inv

    # Step 1: pack groups to nodes
    tokens_per_group = weight.unflatten(-1, (num_groups, group_size)).sum(-1)
    group_pack_index, group_rank_in_pack = balanced_packing(
        tokens_per_group, num_nodes)
    log2mlog = (((group_pack_index * groups_per_node + group_rank_in_pack) *
                 group_size).unsqueeze(-1) +
                torch.arange(group_size,
                             dtype=torch.int64,
                             device=group_pack_index.device)).flatten(-2)
    mlog2log = inverse(log2mlog)

    # Step 2: construct redundant experts within nodes
    # [num_layers * num_nodes, num_logical_experts // num_nodes]
    tokens_per_mlog = weight.gather(-1, mlog2log).view(
        -1, num_logical_experts // num_nodes)
    phy2mlog, phyrank, mlogcnt = replicate_experts(
        tokens_per_mlog, num_physical_experts // num_nodes)

    # Step 3: pack physical_experts to GPUs
    # [num_layers * num_nodes, num_physical_experts // num_nodes]
    tokens_per_phy = (tokens_per_mlog / mlogcnt).gather(-1, phy2mlog)
    pack_index, rank_in_pack = balanced_packing(tokens_per_phy,
                                                num_gpus // num_nodes)
    phy2pphy = pack_index * phy_experts_per_gpu + rank_in_pack
    pphy2phy = inverse(phy2pphy)

    pphy2mlog = phy2mlog.gather(
        -1, pphy2phy)  # [num_layers * num_nodes, num_log_per_nodes]
    pphy2mlog = (pphy2mlog.view(num_layers, num_nodes, -1) + torch.arange(
        0,
        num_logical_experts,
        num_logical_experts // num_nodes,
        device=group_pack_index.device,
    ).view(1, -1, 1)).flatten(-2)
    pphy2log = mlog2log.gather(-1, pphy2mlog)
    pphyrank = phyrank.gather(-1, pphy2phy).view(num_layers, -1)
    logcnt = mlogcnt.view(num_layers, -1).gather(-1, log2mlog)
    return pphy2log, pphyrank, logcnt


def rebalance_experts(
    weight: torch.Tensor,
    num_replicas: int,
    num_groups: int,
    num_nodes: int,
    num_gpus: int,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Entry point for expert-parallelism load balancer.

    Parameters:
        weight: [layers, num_logical_experts], the load statistics for all
            logical experts
        num_replicas: number of physical experts, must be a multiple of
            `num_gpus`
        num_groups: number of expert groups
        num_nodes: number of server nodes, where the intra-node network
            (e.g, NVLink) is faster
        num_gpus: number of GPUs, must be a multiple of `num_nodes`

    Returns:
        physical_to_logical_map: [layers, num_replicas], the expert index of
            each replica
        logical_to_physical_map: [layers, num_logical_experts, X], the replica
            indices for each expert
        expert_count: [layers, num_logical_experts], number of physical
            replicas for each logical expert
    """
    num_layers, num_logical_experts = weight.shape
    weight = weight.float().cpu()
    if num_groups % num_nodes == 0:
        # use hierarchical load-balance policy
        phy2log, phyrank, logcnt = rebalance_experts_hierarchical(
            weight, num_replicas, num_groups, num_nodes, num_gpus)
    else:
        # use global load-balance policy
        phy2log, phyrank, logcnt = rebalance_experts_hierarchical(
            weight, num_replicas, 1, 1, num_gpus)
    num_redundant_experts = num_replicas - num_logical_experts
    maxlogcnt = num_redundant_experts + 1
    log2phy: torch.Tensor = torch.full(
        (num_layers, num_logical_experts, maxlogcnt),
        -1,
        dtype=torch.int64,
        device=logcnt.device,
    )
    log2phy.view(num_layers, -1).scatter_(
        -1,
        phy2log * maxlogcnt + phyrank,
        torch.arange(num_replicas, dtype=torch.int64,
                     device=log2phy.device).expand(num_layers, -1),
    )
    return phy2log, log2phy, logcnt

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""
Expert parallelism load balancer (EPLB) for vLLM.

This module implements the core rearrangement algorithm.

The rearrangement algorithm is adapted from
[DeepSeek EPLB](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/eplb).

Please find at [#12](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/EPLB/issues/12) an example
on how the EPLB algorithm works.
"""

# EVOLVE-BLOCK-START

import torch


def _refine_packing(weight: torch.Tensor, pack_index: torch.Tensor,
                    num_packs: int, max_iters: int = 8) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Bounded vectorized pairwise-swap local search.

    Per row per iteration: find the most/least loaded packs, pick the
    lightest item in the light pack and the item in the heavy pack whose
    weight best splits the gap, and swap them iff it strictly reduces the
    spread. Cardinality is preserved (pure swaps). Small iteration cap
    keeps runtime negligible while shrinking residual imbalance.
    """
    n, m = pack_index.shape
    loads = torch.zeros(n, num_packs, dtype=weight.dtype)
    loads.scatter_add_(1, pack_index, weight)
    rows = torch.arange(n)
    inf = weight.new_full((), float('inf'))
    for _ in range(max_iters):
        pmax = loads.argmax(-1)
        pmin = loads.argmin(-1)
        gap = loads[rows, pmax] - loads[rows, pmin]
        b = torch.where(pack_index == pmin.unsqueeze(-1), weight,
                        inf.expand_as(weight)).argmin(-1)
        wb = weight[rows, b]
        target = (gap / 2 + wb).unsqueeze(-1)
        a = (torch.where(pack_index == pmax.unsqueeze(-1), weight,
                         inf.expand_as(weight)) - target).abs().argmin(-1)
        wa = weight[rows, a]
        improve = (wa > wb) & (2 * (wa - wb) < gap)
        if not improve.any():
            break
        r = improve.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
        pack_index[r, a[r]] = pmin[r]
        pack_index[r, b[r]] = pmax[r]
        loads[r, pmax[r]] += wb[r] - wa[r]
        loads[r, pmin[r]] += wa[r] - wb[r]
    return pack_index


def balanced_packing(weight: torch.Tensor,
                     num_packs: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Pack n weighted objects to m packs, such that each bin contains exactly
    n/m objects and the weights of all packs are as balanced as possible.

    Approach: fully vectorized LPT-style "serpentine" packing.
    Items are sorted by weight (descending), then dealt into packs block by
    block, alternating the pack order in consecutive blocks (0..m-1, then
    m-1..0, ...). This gives each pack exactly n/m items and approximates
    greedy least-loaded assignment at a fraction of the cost (one sort +
    one scatter, no per-item Python loop).

    Parameters:
        weight: [X, n], the weight of each item
        num_packs: number of packs

    Returns:
        pack_index: [X, n], the pack index of each item
        rank_in_pack: [X, n], the rank of the item in the pack
    """
    num_layers, num_groups = weight.shape
    assert num_groups % num_packs == 0
    groups_per_pack = num_groups // num_packs

    if groups_per_pack == 1:
        pack_index = torch.arange(weight.size(-1),
                                  dtype=torch.int64,
                                  device=weight.device).expand(weight.shape)
        rank_in_pack = torch.zeros_like(weight, dtype=torch.int64)
        return pack_index, rank_in_pack

    # Sort items by weight, descending.
    indices = weight.float().sort(-1, descending=True).indices
    # Deal sorted items into blocks of num_packs; alternate block direction
    # (serpentine) so heavy items in consecutive blocks land on different
    # packs, approximating the greedy least-loaded strategy.
    blocks = indices.view(num_layers, groups_per_pack, num_packs)
    pack_seq = torch.arange(num_packs, dtype=torch.int64,
                            device=weight.device)
    pack_pattern = pack_seq.view(1, 1, -1).expand(
        num_layers, groups_per_pack, num_packs).clone()
    # Reverse pack order on odd blocks.
    flip_mask = (torch.arange(groups_per_pack, device=weight.device) % 2 == 1)
    pack_pattern[:, flip_mask] = pack_pattern[:, flip_mask].flip(-1)
    rank_pattern = torch.arange(groups_per_pack, dtype=torch.int64,
                                device=weight.device).view(
                                    1, -1, 1).expand_as(pack_pattern)
    pack_sorted = pack_pattern.reshape(num_layers, num_groups)
    rank_sorted = rank_pattern.reshape(num_layers, num_groups)
    # Scatter back to original item positions.
    pack_index = torch.empty(num_layers, num_groups, dtype=torch.int64,
                             device=weight.device)
    pack_index.scatter_(1, indices, pack_sorted)
    # Bounded local search to shrink the residual load spread.
    pack_index = _refine_packing(weight, pack_index, num_packs)
    # Rebuild ranks so (pack_index, rank_in_pack) is a bijection onto
    # (pack, 0..groups_per_pack-1) after the swaps.
    item_ar = torch.arange(num_groups, dtype=torch.int64,
                           device=weight.device)
    order = (pack_index * num_groups + item_ar).argsort(-1)
    rank_in_pack = torch.empty_like(pack_index)
    rank_in_pack.scatter_(
        1, order,
        (item_ar % groups_per_pack).unsqueeze(0).expand(num_layers,
                                                        num_groups))
    return pack_index, rank_in_pack


def replicate_experts(
        weight: torch.Tensor,
        num_phy: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Replicate `num_log` experts to `num_phy` replicas, such that the maximum
    load of all replicas is minimized.

    Parameters:
        weight: [X, num_log]
        num_phy: total number of experts after replication

    Returns:
        phy2log: [X, num_phy], logical expert id of each physical expert
        rank: [X, num_phy], the replica rank
        logcnt: [X, num_log], number of replicas for each logical expert
    """
    n, num_log = weight.shape
    num_redundant = num_phy - num_log
    assert num_redundant >= 0
    device = weight.device
    phy2log = torch.arange(num_phy, dtype=torch.int64,
                           device=device).repeat(n, 1)
    rank = torch.zeros(n, num_phy, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    logcnt = torch.ones(n, num_log, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    arangen = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    # Water-filling: repeatedly give a replica to the logical expert whose
    # current per-replica load (weight / replicas) is highest. This
    # minimizes the maximum per-replica load. The loop is over redundant
    # experts only (usually small), and each iteration is a single
    # vectorized op over all layers.
    w = weight.float()
    for i in range(num_log, num_phy):
        per_replica_load = w / logcnt
        redundant_indices = per_replica_load.max(dim=-1).indices
        phy2log[:, i] = redundant_indices
        rank[:, i] = logcnt[arangen, redundant_indices]
        logcnt[arangen, redundant_indices] += 1
    return phy2log, rank, logcnt


def rebalance_experts_hierarchical(
    weight: torch.Tensor,
    num_physical_experts: int,
    num_groups: int,
    num_nodes: int,
    num_gpus: int,
):
    """
    Parameters:
        weight: [num_moe_layers, num_logical_experts]
        num_physical_experts: number of physical experts after replication
        num_groups: number of expert groups
        num_nodes: number of server nodes, where the intra-node network
        (e.g, NVLink) is faster
        num_gpus: number of GPUs, must be a multiple of `num_nodes`

    Returns:
        physical_to_logical_map: [num_moe_layers, num_physical_experts]
        logical_to_physical_map: [num_moe_layers, num_logical_experts, X]
        logical_count: [num_moe_layers, num_logical_experts]
    """
    num_layers, num_logical_experts = weight.shape
    assert num_logical_experts % num_groups == 0
    group_size = num_logical_experts // num_groups
    assert num_groups % num_nodes == 0
    groups_per_node = num_groups // num_nodes
    assert num_gpus % num_nodes == 0
    assert num_physical_experts % num_gpus == 0
    phy_experts_per_gpu = num_physical_experts // num_gpus

    def inverse(perm: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        inv = torch.empty_like(perm)
        inv.scatter_(
            1,
            perm,
            torch.arange(perm.size(1), dtype=torch.int64,
                         device=perm.device).expand(perm.shape),
        )
        return inv

    # Step 1: pack groups to nodes
    tokens_per_group = weight.unflatten(-1, (num_groups, group_size)).sum(-1)
    group_pack_index, group_rank_in_pack = balanced_packing(
        tokens_per_group, num_nodes)
    log2mlog = (((group_pack_index * groups_per_node + group_rank_in_pack) *
                 group_size).unsqueeze(-1) +
                torch.arange(group_size,
                             dtype=torch.int64,
                             device=group_pack_index.device)).flatten(-2)
    mlog2log = inverse(log2mlog)

    # Step 2: construct redundant experts within nodes
    # [num_layers * num_nodes, num_logical_experts // num_nodes]
    tokens_per_mlog = weight.gather(-1, mlog2log).view(
        -1, num_logical_experts // num_nodes)
    phy2mlog, phyrank, mlogcnt = replicate_experts(
        tokens_per_mlog, num_physical_experts // num_nodes)

    # Step 3: pack physical_experts to GPUs
    # [num_layers * num_nodes, num_physical_experts // num_nodes]
    tokens_per_phy = (tokens_per_mlog / mlogcnt).gather(-1, phy2mlog)
    pack_index, rank_in_pack = balanced_packing(tokens_per_phy,
                                                num_gpus // num_nodes)

def _try_threshold_pack(w_sorted: torch.Tensor, threshold: float,
                        slots_per_pack: int,
                        num_packs: int) -> torch.Tensor | None:
    """
    Feasibility check for a load threshold `threshold`.

    Items (rows of `w_sorted`, already sorted descending) are placed one at
    a time onto the least-loaded pack that (a) still has a free slot and
    (b) would stay at or below `threshold` after receiving the item. The
    loop is over items only; every op inside is vectorized across all rows
    (layers). Returns the pack index per sorted item, or None if any row
    cannot place all items under the threshold. Cardinality is exact by
    construction: all n = num_packs * slots_per_pack items are placed and
    no pack exceeds its slot budget.
    """
    x, n = w_sorted.shape
    device = w_sorted.device
    loads = torch.zeros(x, num_packs, dtype=w_sorted.dtype, device=device)
    counts = torch.zeros(x, num_packs, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    pack_sorted = torch.full((x, n), -1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    rows = torch.arange(x, device=device)
    big = torch.full_like(loads, float('inf'))
    eps = 1e-9
    for t in range(n):
        w_t = w_sorted[:, t:t + 1]
        elig = (counts < slots_per_pack) & (loads + w_t <= threshold + eps)
        if not bool(elig.any(-1).all()):
            return None
        j = torch.where(elig, loads, big).argmin(-1)
        pack_sorted[:, t] = j
        loads[rows, j] += w_sorted[:, t]
        counts[rows, j] += 1
    return pack_sorted
